1	# Repository Parallelizer
     2	
     3	Manage multiple related git repositories as a single project — with parallel workspaces, branch orchestration, and a web-based GUI.
     4	
     5	## What Is This?
     6	
     7	When a project spans several git repositories, keeping them in sync is tedious: cloning each one, switching branches across all of them, remembering which repos belong together. **Repository Parallelizer** treats a group of repos as one "project" and lets you create isolated **workspaces** — each with its own branch configuration, cloned copies, and a ready-to-open VS Code `.code-workspace` file.
     8	
     9	Set up a project once, then spin up as many parallel workspaces as you need — one for the main branch, one for a feature, one for a hotfix — without stepping on your own toes.
    10	
    11	## Features
    12	
    13	- **Project-based repo grouping** — register repositories once, then combine them into projects.
    14	- **Parallel workspaces** — create multiple independent workspaces per project, each with its own branch assignments and cloned copies.
    15	- **One-click branch switching** — switch branches across all repos in a workspace in a single operation, with conflict detection.
    16	- **VS Code integration** — auto-generated `.code-workspace` files let you open an entire workspace in VS Code instantly.
    17	- **Web GUI** — a built-in browser UI for managing repositories, projects, workspaces, and branches — no terminal required after setup. The project dashboard supports real-time filtering by name/ID/description, repository filtering, and sort by alphabetical or last-activity order.
    18	- **Live git status** — automatic polling shows current branches, uncommitted changes, and unfetched commits at a glance.
    19	- **Workspace health checks** — detect and fix configuration drift (missing repos, stale workspace files).
    20	- **Interactive CLI** — a keyboard-driven terminal menu for quick access to setup, server launch, and documentation generation.
    21	- **Private repo support** — per-host credential management for cloning private repositories.
    22	
    23	## How Does This Compare to Git Worktrees?
    24	
    25	Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches of a **single** repository side by side — great when your entire project lives in one repo. Repository Parallelizer solves a different problem: when your project spans **multiple** repositories that need to move together.
    26	
    27	| | Git Worktrees | Repository Parallelizer |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| **Scope** | One repository, multiple branches | Multiple repositories, multiple branches |
    30	| **Branch switching** | Per-repo only | Coordinated across all repos at once |
    31	| **VS Code workspace** | Manual setup | Auto-generated `.code-workspace` files |
    32	| **Status overview** | Per-repo (`git status`) | Aggregated across all repos in a workspace |
    33	
    34	If your project is a single repo, worktrees are the simpler choice. If you're juggling a frontend, backend, shared library, and infrastructure repo that all need to be on the same feature branch — that's where this tool comes in.
    35	
    36	## Requirements
    37	
    38	- **Node.js** >= 18
    39	- **npm** >= 9
    40	- **git** >= 2.28
    41	
    42	## Quick Start
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	# Clone and build
    46	git clone https://github.com/Mistralys/repo-parallelizer.git
    47	cd repo-parallelizer
    48	npm install
    49	npm run build
    50	
    51	# Run the setup wizard to create your config
    52	npm link
    53	paralizer setup
    54	
    55	# Launch the GUI
    56	paralizer serve
    57	```
    58	
    59	The setup wizard walks you through creating a `config.json` with your projects folder and storage location. Once complete, open `http://localhost:4200` in your browser to start managing your repositories.
    60	
    61	### Alternative: run without installing globally
    62	
    63	```bash
    64	# Unix / macOS
    65	./menu.sh
    66	
    67	# Windows
    68	menu.cmd
    69	```
    70	
    71	### CLI commands
    72	
    73	| Command | Description |
    74	|---------|-------------|
    75	| `paralizer` | Open the interactive CLI menu |
    76	| `paralizer serve` | Start the GUI server directly |
    77	| `paralizer setup` | Run the setup wizard |
    78	| `paralizer docs` | Generate project documentation |
    79	
    80	## Start with Windows
    81	
    82	1. Press `Win + R`, type the following command to open your user Startup folder, and press **Enter**:
    83	   ```
    84	   shell:startup
    85	   ```
    86	   *(This opens the folder: `C:\Users\<YourUsername>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`)*
    87	
    88	2. In that folder, right-click an empty area and select **New** > **Text Document**.
    89	3. Name it `start-repo-parallelizer.vbs` (ensure you delete the `.txt` extension!).
    90	4. Right-click the new file, select **Edit** (or open it with Notepad/VS Code), and paste the following code into it:
    91	
    92	   ```vbscript
    93	   Set WshShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
    94	   ' 0 means the window will be hidden, so you don't have a lingering terminal
    95	   WshShell.Run "cmd /c paralizer serve", 0
    96	   Set WshShell = Nothing
    97	   ```
    98	
    99	   > **Requires `npm link`** — run `npm link` once in the project folder so `paralizer` is available globally.

1	# GUI Frontend
     2	
     3	The frontend is a vanilla JavaScript SPA with no build step, served as static files by the built-in HTTP server from `gui/public/`.
     4	
     5	## Architecture
     6	
     7	- **Routing:** Hash-based client-side router (`#/path`) with named parameter extraction (`:id`, `:wid`).
     8	- **Module system:** Native ES modules loaded by the browser. No bundler.
     9	- **State management:** None — every view fetches fresh data from the REST API on render. Mutations trigger a full view re-render.
    10	- **Styling:** Pico CSS (classless variant) as base layer, with a custom `styles.css` override layer using CSS custom properties. Light/dark theme switching via `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`.
    11	
    12	## Router
    13	
    14	The `Router` class (`gui/public/js/router.js`) manages view lifecycle:
    15	
    16	1. Listens for `hashchange` events.
    17	2. Matches the hash against registered patterns.
    18	3. Calls the previous view's cleanup function (if returned).
    19	4. Clears the `#app` container.
    20	5. Calls the matched view function with `(container, params)`.
    21	6. Stores any cleanup function returned by the view.
    22	
    23	## Routes
    24	
    25	| Hash Pattern | View | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|
    27	| `#/` | `dashboard.js` | Project listing with a filter/sort toolbar and a "Create Project" form. The toolbar (`.project-filter-toolbar`) sits between the page header and the project list and contains three labelled controls — each has a visible `<label class="filter-label">` with a `for`/`id` binding: a debounced search input (`id="project-filter-search"`, `type="search"`, ~250 ms), a repository filter `<select id="project-filter-repo">` populated from `api.repositories.list()` (always rendered; disabled with a "No repositories" placeholder when no repos exist or when the fetch fails — a toast is shown on failure), and a sort `<select id="project-filter-sort">` with `alpha` (Alphabetical, default) and `activity` (Last Activity) options. All three controls fire an `onFilterChange(FilterState)` callback on change. The current filter state (`{ search, repoId, sort }`) is maintained in `renderDashboard` and flows into `buildFilterToolbar`, `applyFiltersAndSort`, and `renderProjectGrid`. `applyFiltersAndSort(filterState, allProjects)` is a pure exported function — it receives the project list as an explicit parameter (no closure over module state) and can be unit-tested without DOM involvement. Filter changes re-apply the current state to the in-memory `_allProjects` cache without re-fetching; creating a new project re-fetches all project data from the API and re-applies the current filter/sort state. An empty-state message — "No projects match the current filters." vs "No projects yet." — distinguishes filtered-empty from truly-empty lists. |
    28	| `#/repositories` | `repositories.js` | Repository CRUD table. Each row's **Name** column renders as a clickable `<a class="repo-name-display repo-name-link">` element linking to `#/repositories/${encodeURIComponent(repo.id)}`. Clicking Edit switches the Name cell to an inline `<input>` for in-place editing; Save/Cancel restore the link with updated or original text. |
    29	| `#/repositories/:id` | `repository-detail.js` | Repository overview: table of every workspace across every project that contains the given repository. Each row shows Project (link to `#/projects/:pid`), Workspace (link to `#/projects/:pid/workspaces/:wid`), and the shared Branch/Status/Actions cells from `buildRepoStatusCells`. STABLE workspace rows show plain-text branch names; all other rows have a clickable branch-switch trigger. A "Refresh" button re-discovers the full project/workspace set (calls `api.projects.list()` + the full fan-out) and diffs against the existing rows: new rows are appended, removed rows are dropped, and existing rows are updated in-place via `api.status.refresh()` — protected by a `refreshInProgress` mutex. A 404 response for the repository renders a "not found" message with a link back to `#/repositories`. An empty-state message is shown when no projects contain the repository. Individual project/workspace fetch failures are handled gracefully via `Promise.allSettled` — partial results are displayed and a warning toast is shown when any fetch failed. The webserver URL is fetched once during initial load; the "Browse" button is shown only when `webserverUrl` is configured. `buildRepoStatusCells` is called with an `onError` callback (`(msg) => showToast(msg, 'error')`) so Git GUI button failures are surfaced as toasts without a dynamic `import('./toast.js')` inside the component. |
    30	| `#/projects/:id` | `project-detail.js` | Project metadata, tabbed repo/workspace/danger-zone management. The workspace table includes a **Health** column: initialized workspaces with health issues show a warning badge with issue count; healthy and uninitialized workspaces show an empty cell. Health is fetched in parallel with status for all initialized workspaces via `Promise.allSettled` (graceful degradation — fetch failures leave the health cell empty). |
    31	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` | `workspace-detail.js` | Live git status with countdown-based polling and manual refresh. Health report fetched in parallel on initial load and on every poll/refresh cycle. Unhealthy workspaces render a `.health-alert` card with per-issue rows and fix buttons (`Regenerate File` for `regenerate-workspace-file` issues, `Fix Setup` for `setup-workspace` issues). The header management row includes an **"Open in VS Code"** button (shown only when `workspace.initialized` is `true`; dynamically inserted after a successful Setup without a full re-render). The repository status table has a 4th **"Actions"** column; each repository row contains a **"Browse"** button (shown only when `webserverUrl` is configured, opens `{webserverUrl}/{projectId}/{workspaceId}/{repoId}/` in a new tab via `window.open`) followed by a **"Git GUI"** button that calls `api.workspaces.launch.githubDesktop()`. The webserver URL is fetched once during the initial data load (in parallel with other requests) via `api.config.webserverUrl.get()`. In non-STABLE workspaces, each **Branch** cell is a clickable trigger (`<button class="branch-switch-trigger">`) that opens an inline quick-switch popover via `showBranchQuickSwitch()`. STABLE workspace branch cells remain plain text. `buildRepoStatusCells` is called with an `onError` callback so Git GUI button failures show as toasts. DOM clearing uses `clearElement()` from `utils/dom.js` throughout (no `innerHTML = ''` assignments). A **Notes** section (built by `buildNotesSection()`) is appended below the repository status table: it contains a `<textarea id="workspace-notes-textarea">` pre-populated from `workspace.notes`, a 1000 ms debounced `input` listener that calls `api.workspaces.update()`, and an `aria-live="polite"` status span that shows "Saving…" / "Saved" / "Save failed." feedback. |
    32	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branch-switch` | `branch-switch.js` | 3-step branch switch wizard. |
    33	| `#/settings` | `settings.js` | Settings view with four sections: **Git Credentials** (add/delete per-host PATs), **Repositories Refresh Delay** (configurable `gitPollingIntervalSeconds`), **Webserver URL** (base URL of the local webserver; enables the "Browse" button in the workspace-detail view), and **Notes Display** (card height in px and column count for the notes grid, backed by `GET/PUT /api/config/notes-display`). All non-credentials sections share a single **"Save Settings"** footer button that calls each section's `save()` function in parallel via `Promise.all()`. The Notes Display section is built by `buildNotesDisplaySection()`, which uses CSS classes `notes-display-section` (section wrapper), `notes-display-input-row` (flex row for label + input + unit), `notes-display-label` (label element), `notes-display-input` (number input), and `notes-display-unit` (unit span, e.g. "px"). |
    34	| `#/error-log` | `error-log.js` | Paginated, filterable error log table with expandable detail rows and "Clear All" action. |
    35	| `#/notes` | `notes-collected.js` | Two-panel notes view: a left sidebar listing all workspaces grouped by collapsible project groups (workspaces with notes carry a `.has-notes` class and a blue dot indicator), and a right scrollable main panel of editable note cards. On initial load only workspaces with non-empty notes show cards. Clicking a sidebar item for a workspace with a card scrolls the main panel to it; clicking one without a card creates a new empty card and focuses the textarea. Each card header contains a clickable workspace ID link to `#/projects/:pid/workspaces/:wid`. Textareas auto-save after 1000 ms of inactivity via `api.workspaces.update()`; saving empty text removes the card and clears the sidebar indicator. A `.notes-empty-state` message is shown when no cards are present. |
    36	
    37	## API Client
    38	
    39	`api.js` exports a namespaced `api` object with eight top-level groups:
    40	
    41	- `api.repositories` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `delete(id)`
    42	- `api.projects` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `rename(id, newId)`, `delete(id)`, `addRepository(pid, rid)`, `removeRepository(pid, rid)`
    43	- `api.workspaces` — `list(pid)`, `get(pid, wid)`, `create(pid, data)`, `update(pid, wid, data)`, `rename(pid, wid, newId)`, `delete(pid, wid)`, `setup(pid, wid)`, `health(pid, wid)`, `regenerateFile(pid, wid)`, `launch.vscode(pid, wid)`, `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)`
    44	- `api.branches` — `list(pid, wid)`, `switch(pid, wid, assignments)`
    45	- `api.status` — `get(pid, wid)`, `refresh(pid, wid)`
    46	- `api.config.credentials` — `list()`, `set(data)`, `delete(host)`
    47	- `api.config.polling` — `get()`, `set(seconds)`
    48	- `api.config.webserverUrl` — `get()`, `set(url)`
    49	- `api.config.notesDisplay` — `get()`, `set(data)`
    50	- `api.errorLog` — `list(params?)`, `get(id)`, `clear()`, `count()`
    51	- `api.notes` — `list()`
    52	
    53	### `api.workspaces` — Health & File Methods
    54	
    55	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    56	|---|---|---|
    57	| `health(pid, wid)` | `GET /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/health` | Fetch the health report for an initialized workspace. Returns `{ healthy: boolean, issues: Array<{ type: string, severity: string, message: string, fixAction: string, repositoryId?: string }> }`. |
    58	| `regenerateFile(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/regenerate-workspace-file` | Regenerate the `.code-workspace` file from the current repository list without cloning. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. |
    59	
    60	**`health()` issue `fixAction` values:**
    61	- `regenerate-workspace-file` — missing or stale `.code-workspace` file; surface a `Regenerate File` button.
    62	- `setup-workspace` — uncloned repository; surface a `Fix Setup` button.
    63	
    64	### `api.workspaces.launch` — External-App Launch Methods
    65	
    66	External-application launchers are grouped under the `api.workspaces.launch` sub-namespace. New launcher methods (e.g. "Open in Terminal") should be added here rather than as flat methods on `api.workspaces`.
    67	
    68	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    69	|---|---|---|
    70	| `launch.vscode(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` | Open the workspace's `.code-workspace` file in VS Code. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the workspace file does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-vscode'`). |
    71	| `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` | Open a repository's local clone directory in GitHub Desktop. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the repository directory does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-github-desktop'`). |
    72	
    73	**Caller contract:** All path parameters (`pid`, `wid`, `rid`) are passed through `encodeURIComponent` inside `api.js`. Callers are responsible for validating that these values are not `undefined`/`null` before invoking these methods — `encodeURIComponent` will coerce them to the strings `'undefined'`/`'null'` rather than throwing.
    74	
    75	### `api.errorLog` Reference
    76	
    77	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    78	|---|---|---|
    79	| `list(params?)` | `GET /api/error-log[?...]` | Fetch error log entries with optional filtering and pagination. |
    80	| `get(id)` | `GET /api/error-log/:id` | Fetch a single entry by numeric ID. |
    81	| `clear()` | `DELETE /api/error-log` | Delete all entries. Resolves with `undefined` on HTTP 204. |
    82	| `count()` | `GET /api/error-log?limit=0` | Fetch only the total count (no entries payload). Useful for badges. |
    83	
    84	**`list()` params shape:**
    85	
    86	```js
    87	api.errorLog.list({
    88	    severity: 'error',   // optional — 'error' | 'warning'
    89	    source:   'clone',   // optional — exact-match on Source field
    90	    limit:    10,        // optional — max entries to return (default 100 server-side)
    91	    offset:   0,         // optional — zero-based page offset
    92	})
    93	```
    94	
    95	All params are optional. Omitting `params` entirely (or passing `undefined`) sends a bare `GET /api/error-log`.
    96	
    97	**`clear()` 204 contract:** The underlying `request()` helper resolves with `undefined` when the server returns HTTP 204 (no body). Callers should not try to read a response value from `clear()`.
    98	
    99	**`count()` pattern:** Sends `GET /api/error-log?limit=0`. The server returns `{ entries: [], total: N }`. Read `response.total` for the count. This is the recommended approach for polling a badge counter without transferring entry data.

1	# GUI Frontend
     2	
     3	The frontend is a vanilla JavaScript SPA with no build step, served as static files by the built-in HTTP server from `gui/public/`.
     4	
     5	## Architecture
     6	
     7	- **Routing:** Hash-based client-side router (`#/path`) with named parameter extraction (`:id`, `:wid`).
     8	- **Module system:** Native ES modules loaded by the browser. No bundler.
     9	- **State management:** None — every view fetches fresh data from the REST API on render. Mutations trigger a full view re-render.
    10	- **Styling:** Pico CSS (classless variant) as base layer, with a custom `styles.css` override layer using CSS custom properties. Light/dark theme switching via `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`.
    11	
    12	## Router
    13	
    14	The `Router` class (`gui/public/js/router.js`) manages view lifecycle:
    15	
    16	1. Listens for `hashchange` events.
    17	2. Matches the hash against registered patterns.
    18	3. Calls the previous view's cleanup function (if returned).
    19	4. Clears the `#app` container.
    20	5. Calls the matched view function with `(container, params)`.
    21	6. Stores any cleanup function returned by the view.
    22	
    23	## Routes
    24	
    25	| Hash Pattern | View | Description |
    26	|---|---|---|
    27	| `#/` | `dashboard.js` | Project listing with a filter/sort toolbar and a "Create Project" form. The toolbar (`.project-filter-toolbar`) sits between the page header and the project list and contains three labelled controls — each has a visible `<label class="filter-label">` with a `for`/`id` binding: a debounced search input (`id="project-filter-search"`, `type="search"`, ~250 ms), a repository filter `<select id="project-filter-repo">` populated from `api.repositories.list()` (always rendered; disabled with a "No repositories" placeholder when no repos exist or when the fetch fails — a toast is shown on failure), and a sort `<select id="project-filter-sort">` with `alpha` (Alphabetical, default) and `activity` (Last Activity) options. All three controls fire an `onFilterChange(FilterState)` callback on change. The current filter state (`{ search, repoId, sort }`) is maintained in `renderDashboard` and flows into `buildFilterToolbar`, `applyFiltersAndSort`, and `renderProjectGrid`. `applyFiltersAndSort(filterState, allProjects)` is a pure exported function — it receives the project list as an explicit parameter (no closure over module state) and can be unit-tested without DOM involvement. Filter changes re-apply the current state to the in-memory `_allProjects` cache without re-fetching; creating a new project re-fetches all project data from the API and re-applies the current filter/sort state. An empty-state message — "No projects match the current filters." vs "No projects yet." — distinguishes filtered-empty from truly-empty lists. |
    28	| `#/repositories` | `repositories.js` | Repository CRUD table. Each row's **Name** column renders as a clickable `<a class="repo-name-display repo-name-link">` element linking to `#/repositories/${encodeURIComponent(repo.id)}`. Clicking Edit switches the Name cell to an inline `<input>` for in-place editing; Save/Cancel restore the link with updated or original text. |
    29	| `#/repositories/:id` | `repository-detail.js` | Repository overview: table of every workspace across every project that contains the given repository. Each row shows Project (link to `#/projects/:pid`), Workspace (link to `#/projects/:pid/workspaces/:wid`), and the shared Branch/Status/Actions cells from `buildRepoStatusCells`. STABLE workspace rows show plain-text branch names; all other rows have a clickable branch-switch trigger. A "Refresh" button re-discovers the full project/workspace set (calls `api.projects.list()` + the full fan-out) and diffs against the existing rows: new rows are appended, removed rows are dropped, and existing rows are updated in-place via `api.status.refresh()` — protected by a `refreshInProgress` mutex. A 404 response for the repository renders a "not found" message with a link back to `#/repositories`. An empty-state message is shown when no projects contain the repository. Individual project/workspace fetch failures are handled gracefully via `Promise.allSettled` — partial results are displayed and a warning toast is shown when any fetch failed. The webserver URL is fetched once during initial load; the "Browse" button is shown only when `webserverUrl` is configured. `buildRepoStatusCells` is called with an `onError` callback (`(msg) => showToast(msg, 'error')`) so Git GUI button failures are surfaced as toasts without a dynamic `import('./toast.js')` inside the component. |
    30	| `#/projects/:id` | `project-detail.js` | Project metadata, tabbed repo/workspace/danger-zone management. The workspace table includes a **Health** column: initialized workspaces with health issues show a warning badge with issue count; healthy and uninitialized workspaces show an empty cell. Health is fetched in parallel with status for all initialized workspaces via `Promise.allSettled` (graceful degradation — fetch failures leave the health cell empty). |
    31	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid` | `workspace-detail.js` | Live git status with countdown-based polling and manual refresh. Health report fetched in parallel on initial load and on every poll/refresh cycle. Unhealthy workspaces render a `.health-alert` card with per-issue rows and fix buttons (`Regenerate File` for `regenerate-workspace-file` issues, `Fix Setup` for `setup-workspace` issues). The header management row includes an **"Open in VS Code"** button (shown only when `workspace.initialized` is `true`; dynamically inserted after a successful Setup without a full re-render). The repository status table has a 4th **"Actions"** column; each repository row contains a **"Browse"** button (shown only when `webserverUrl` is configured, opens `{webserverUrl}/{projectId}/{workspaceId}/{repoId}/` in a new tab via `window.open`) followed by a **"Git GUI"** button that calls `api.workspaces.launch.githubDesktop()`. The webserver URL is fetched once during the initial data load (in parallel with other requests) via `api.config.webserverUrl.get()`. In non-STABLE workspaces, each **Branch** cell is a clickable trigger (`<button class="branch-switch-trigger">`) that opens an inline quick-switch popover via `showBranchQuickSwitch()`. STABLE workspace branch cells remain plain text. `buildRepoStatusCells` is called with an `onError` callback so Git GUI button failures show as toasts. DOM clearing uses `clearElement()` from `utils/dom.js` throughout (no `innerHTML = ''` assignments). A **Notes** section (built by `buildNotesSection()`) is appended below the repository status table: it contains a `<textarea id="workspace-notes-textarea">` pre-populated from `workspace.notes`, a 1000 ms debounced `input` listener that calls `api.workspaces.update()`, and an `aria-live="polite"` status span that shows "Saving…" / "Saved" / "Save failed." feedback. |
    32	| `#/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/branch-switch` | `branch-switch.js` | 3-step branch switch wizard. |
    33	| `#/settings` | `settings.js` | Settings view with four sections: **Git Credentials** (add/delete per-host PATs), **Repositories Refresh Delay** (configurable `gitPollingIntervalSeconds`), **Webserver URL** (base URL of the local webserver; enables the "Browse" button in the workspace-detail view), and **Notes Display** (card height in px and column count for the notes grid, backed by `GET/PUT /api/config/notes-display`). All non-credentials sections share a single **"Save Settings"** footer button that calls each section's `save()` function in parallel via `Promise.all()`. The Notes Display section is built by `buildNotesDisplaySection()`, which uses CSS classes `notes-display-section` (section wrapper), `notes-display-input-row` (flex row for label + input + unit), `notes-display-label` (label element), `notes-display-input` (number input), and `notes-display-unit` (unit span, e.g. "px"). |
    34	| `#/error-log` | `error-log.js` | Paginated, filterable error log table with expandable detail rows and "Clear All" action. |
    35	| `#/notes` | `notes-collected.js` | Two-panel notes view: a left sidebar listing all workspaces grouped by collapsible project groups (workspaces with notes carry a `.has-notes` class and a blue dot indicator), and a right scrollable main panel of editable note cards. On initial load only workspaces with non-empty notes show cards. Clicking a sidebar item for a workspace with a card scrolls the main panel to it; clicking one without a card creates a new empty card and focuses the textarea. Each card header contains a clickable workspace ID link to `#/projects/:pid/workspaces/:wid`. Textareas auto-save after 1000 ms of inactivity via `api.workspaces.update()`; saving empty text removes the card and clears the sidebar indicator. A `.notes-empty-state` message is shown when no cards are present. |
    36	
    37	> **Maintainer note — Settings sections:** `settings.js` has a module-level JSDoc block (at the top of the file) that lists all active settings sections. When adding or removing a `build*Section()` factory from `settings.js`, update that JSDoc list to keep it in sync with the route description in this table.
    38	
    39	## API Client
    40	
    41	`api.js` exports a namespaced `api` object with eight top-level groups:
    42	
    43	- `api.repositories` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `delete(id)`
    44	- `api.projects` — `list()`, `get(id)`, `create(data)`, `update(id, data)`, `rename(id, newId)`, `delete(id)`, `addRepository(pid, rid)`, `removeRepository(pid, rid)`
    45	- `api.workspaces` — `list(pid)`, `get(pid, wid)`, `create(pid, data)`, `update(pid, wid, data)`, `rename(pid, wid, newId)`, `delete(pid, wid)`, `setup(pid, wid)`, `health(pid, wid)`, `regenerateFile(pid, wid)`, `launch.vscode(pid, wid)`, `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)`
    46	- `api.branches` — `list(pid, wid)`, `switch(pid, wid, assignments)`
    47	- `api.status` — `get(pid, wid)`, `refresh(pid, wid)`
    48	- `api.config.credentials` — `list()`, `set(data)`, `delete(host)`
    49	- `api.config.polling` — `get()`, `set(seconds)`
    50	- `api.config.webserverUrl` — `get()`, `set(url)`
    51	- `api.config.notesDisplay` — `get()`, `set(data)`
    52	- `api.errorLog` — `list(params?)`, `get(id)`, `clear()`, `count()`
    53	- `api.notes` — `list()`
    54	
    55	### `api.workspaces` — Health & File Methods
    56	
    57	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    58	|---|---|---|
    59	| `health(pid, wid)` | `GET /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/health` | Fetch the health report for an initialized workspace. Returns `{ healthy: boolean, issues: Array<{ type: string, severity: string, message: string, fixAction: string, repositoryId?: string }> }`. |
    60	| `regenerateFile(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/regenerate-workspace-file` | Regenerate the `.code-workspace` file from the current repository list without cloning. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. |
    61	
    62	**`health()` issue `fixAction` values:**
    63	- `regenerate-workspace-file` — missing or stale `.code-workspace` file; surface a `Regenerate File` button.
    64	- `setup-workspace` — uncloned repository; surface a `Fix Setup` button.
    65	
    66	### `api.workspaces.launch` — External-App Launch Methods
    67	
    68	External-application launchers are grouped under the `api.workspaces.launch` sub-namespace. New launcher methods (e.g. "Open in Terminal") should be added here rather than as flat methods on `api.workspaces`.
    69	
    70	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    71	|---|---|---|
    72	| `launch.vscode(pid, wid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/vscode` | Open the workspace's `.code-workspace` file in VS Code. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the workspace file does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-vscode'`). |
    73	| `launch.githubDesktop(pid, wid, rid)` | `POST /api/projects/:id/workspaces/:wid/launch/github-desktop/:rid` | Open a repository's local clone directory in GitHub Desktop. No request body. Returns `{ success: boolean }`. 400 if the repository directory does not exist on disk (run setup first). 500 on OS-level spawn failure (logged under Source: `'app-launcher'`, Operation: `'launch-github-desktop'`). |
    74	
    75	**Caller contract:** All path parameters (`pid`, `wid`, `rid`) are passed through `encodeURIComponent` inside `api.js`. Callers are responsible for validating that these values are not `undefined`/`null` before invoking these methods — `encodeURIComponent` will coerce them to the strings `'undefined'`/`'null'` rather than throwing.
    76	
    77	### `api.errorLog` Reference
    78	
    79	| Method | HTTP | Description |
    80	|---|---|---|
    81	| `list(params?)` | `GET /api/error-log[?...]` | Fetch error log entries with optional filtering and pagination. |
    82	| `get(id)` | `GET /api/error-log/:id` | Fetch a single entry by numeric ID. |
    83	| `clear()` | `DELETE /api/error-log` | Delete all entries. Resolves with `undefined` on HTTP 204. |
    84	| `count()` | `GET /api/error-log?limit=0` | Fetch only the total count (no entries payload). Useful for badges. |
    85	
    86	**`list()` params shape:**
    87	
    88	```js
    89	api.errorLog.list({
    90	    severity: 'error',   // optional — 'error' | 'warning'
    91	    source:   'clone',   // optional — exact-match on Source field
    92	    limit:    10,        // optional — max entries to return (default 100 server-side)
    93	    offset:   0,         // optional — zero-based page offset
    94	})
    95	```
    96	
    97	All params are optional. Omitting `params` entirely (or passing `undefined`) sends a bare `GET /api/error-log`.
    98	
    99	**`clear()` 204 contract:** The underlying `request()` helper resolves with `undefined` when the server returns HTTP 204 (no body). Callers should not try to read a response value from `clear()`.
